statement_spans.label: author lemma environment with its own label lemma-picard-stack-open-in-coh (no canonical tag in the snapshot tag list); statement at source lines 2817-2826

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: the map sends the triple (T, g, L) of the Picard stack to the same triple viewed in the coherent stack situation, which makes sense because L is finitely presented, flat over T (base change of flatness) and has proper support (base change of properness); the content is: for an object (T, g, F) of the coherent stack there is an open U in T such that (a) factoring through U is equivalent to (b) F_{T'} being invertible; take W the open locus where F is finite locally free (commuting with base change), replace T by T minus the image of the complement of W, where F is finite locally free, and use the disjoint union decomposition into rank-i loci to define U as the complement of the image of the loci of rank other than 1 (open because quasi-compact T gives finitely many nonempty pieces) (source lines 2828-2874)

core_obligations: The map makes sense (proof lines 2829-2838): L is finitely presented, flat over T, and proper support, by the two base-change lemmas.
Reformulation (proof lines 2842-2852): the content is the open U with (a) iff (b).

Construction of U (proof lines 2853-2874): W the finite-locally-free locus (open, base-change compatible); reduce to F finite locally free; the rank decomposition X_T = disjoint union X_i and U = complement of the image of the rank-not-1 pieces, open by quasi-compactness.
proof_roadmap: Verify the map lands in the coherent stack (proof lines 2829-2838).
State the equivalent characterization of the desired open U (proof lines 2842-2852).
Build U from the finite-locally-free locus W and the rank decomposition (proof lines 2853-2874).
